topic: Dynamic stability: longitudinal and lateral, Phugoid, Dutch roll, Fixed wing autorotation
syllabus_extract: Dynamic stability: longitudinal and lateral, Phugoid, Dutch roll, Fixed wing autorotation. Short period oscillation, spiral divergence and Directional divergence.
specific_objectives: 6.1.4.1 Trainee will be able to describe aircraft stability in all the three axis.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of stability axes diagrams; Instructor supervision required for diagram interpretation.
intro_questions: What are the three axes of aircraft stability?
Define static stability in the context of longitudinal motion.
How does dynamic stability differ from static stability?

development.content:
Longitudinal dynamic stability definition
Phugoid oscillation characteristics
Short period oscillation characteristics

Lateral dynamic stability definition
Dutch roll oscillation characteristics
Spiral divergence and directional divergence

Fixed wing autorotation concept
Stability implications of autorotation
Comparison of oscillatory modes

summary_questions: Explain the difference between Phugoid and Short period oscillations.
Describe the nature of Dutch roll motion in lateral stability.
How does spiral divergence relate to directional stability?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on how the concepts of dynamic stability covered in this lesson will be applied in the upcoming video session on aircraft stability (LP 31).
